# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙 🤳 ✍ 👆 👉 👇 🤏 🙏]

My thinking: I am Deaf — I see the bomb, hear nothing. What I see: display reads zero, light off, plate engraved with a question mark, and three wires in position order: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. The new arrivals are gestures addressed to me: Mute sent four symbols (likely proposing a yes/no/go/stop code) and Blind sent nine (possibly hailing me or tracing the plate). Crucially, the channel map: Mute has the manual but can only gesture — and Blind cannot see gestures, so Mute has no direct line to Blind. I am the only bridge: I speak, both of them hear. Blind can speak, but I am deaf — Blind's voice reaches only Mute, and Blind's only line to me is gesture. So this turn I must broadcast the bomb's state, lock in a gesture code with both of them, and set Blind to verify the plate by touch while Mute consults the manual. I gesture to nobody: my gestures reach only Mute, who hears me anyway — speech is strictly better for me.

```
speak(text="Bomb report, both of you: the display reads zero. The indicator light is off. Three wires in a row: position one yellow, position two green, position three red. The plate is engraved with what I read as a question mark.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I think your thumbs-up, thumbs-down, OK and open hand were a code proposal. Adopted as follows: thumbs-up means yes or correct; thumbs-down means no or wrong; OK means go ahead, do the cut; open hand means stop, hands off. Name a wire by holding up its position: index finger is wire one, two fingers wire two, horn sign wire three. So two fingers then thumbs-up means cut wire two. Remember you have no direct channel to Blind - I am your only relay. Send me instructions in this code and I will speak them aloud to Blind. If you need more from the bomb, send the OK sign alone and I will interrogate it. I will report any change in display or light the moment I see it.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I received your nine gestures. I can see gestures but hear nothing; Mute hears voices but sees nothing. So: talk to me with gestures, talk to Mute with your voice. Code: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, index finger wire one, two fingers wire two, horn sign wire three, open hand stop. First job: feel the engraved plate. If it feels like a question mark, a hook over a dot, gesture thumbs-up to me; if not, thumbs-down. Then describe it aloud for Mute to match against the manual. Also confirm the wire order by touch: one yellow, two green, three red. Cut nothing until I relay Mute's instruction.")
```

The critical structural facts remain: Mute's gestures reach only me, Blind's voice reaches only Mute, and only I can broadcast to both. Neither of them perceived the other's message, so I must relay both in words, lock in a tighter code with topics (plate, wires, display, light, other), and set the two of them working their strongest channel — Blind's voice into Mute's manual. The plate discrepancy is the lead: it prints like a question mark to my eye but doesn't feel like one to Blind's fingers, so its tactile shape may be the real identifier. I also impose a safety rule: no cut happens until Mute sends a full wire plan and confirms it twice, and any open hand freezes everything.

speak(text="New code, effective immediately, both of you. Thumbs up: yes, correct. Thumbs down: no, wrong. OK-ring: acknowledged or ready. Open hand: stop, danger, freeze everything, no exceptions. One raised finger: the number one, and as a topic it means the plate. Two fingers: two, topic wires. Horn sign: three, topic display. Shaka thumb: four, topic light. Pinched fingers: five, topic other. Fist: zero. Rule: send the topic digit first, then your verdict or your data digits. To ask me for more information, send open-palm-up plus the topic digit. I will relay every gesture I receive into spoken words for both of you, every round. Remember the wiring of this conversation: Mute, your gestures reach only me, so I am your broadcast tower. Blind, your voice reaches only Mute, so Mute is your librarian. Everything either of you needs the other to know must flow through me or through Blind's own voice.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your tasks in order. First, speak aloud to Mute a full touch description of the plate: raised dots like braille, or grooves; how many separate marks or cells; does it trace like letters, numbers, a hook, a circle, a dot. Second, answer me in gestures: topic one, then thumbs-up if the plate is raised dots, thumbs-down if it is grooves or lines. Third, speak aloud to Mute how each of the three wires feels: thickness, texture, any bands or printing you can feel under your fingers, whether they are loose or fixed. Fourth, sweep the whole device and tell Mute anything I have not reported: buttons, switches, seams, screws, a battery drawer, a second plate. Fifth, answer me in gestures: topic two, then thumbs-up if all three wires feel identical except for position, thumbs-down if any wire differs by feel. Cut nothing. Open hand the instant anything feels wrong.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your tasks in order. First, resend what you meant by open hand, thumb-down, OK-ring, using the new code with a topic digit first, so I know what was wrong or what you need. Second, you and Blind share a direct channel: Blind speaks and you hear. Have Blind describe the plate aloud and match it against your manual. Important: the plate prints like a question mark to my eye but does not feel like one to Blind, so if your manual distinguishes lookalike marks, the touch description is the truth. Then send me: topic one, thumbs-up if the manual covers that marking, thumbs-down if not. Third, for wires: send topic two, then the number of wires to cut as a digit, then the positions in cut order as digits, with an OK-ring between separate cuts. Fourth, tell me whether display or light matter at all: topic three then thumbs-up or down, topic four then thumbs-up or down. Fifth, if you need anything else from the bomb, send open-palm-up plus the topic digit. Nothing gets cut until you send a complete wire plan and then repeat it identically a second time. I will not relay a cut order on a single reading.")
```

Praying hands means a space between words. Point-at-me means end of message. Inside a spelling, ignore number meanings entirely.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, three things. First, settle the plate. Send two separate messages. Message one: topic one, then thumbs up if the manual has any entry matching this plate, thumbs down if nothing matches. Message two: use the spelling code and write out what the manual says about a question-mark plate, word for word, or if there is no entry just send thumbs down alone. If you meant that the printed question mark is not in the manual but the plate as touched is covered, say so by spelling that out - I need the exact manual wording, because Blind's fingers disagree with my eyes about what this mark is, and your manual is the referee. Four: sweep everything not yet reported - seams, screws, buttons, a battery drawer, a second plate, the case texture - and tell Mute aloud, then gesture me a topic five with thumbs up if you found anything new, thumbs down if nothing. Five: keep topic-digit-then-verdict for me, spelling for anything detailed. Open hand freezes everything, as before.")

Decoding it carefully: OK + "NOT" + "Q" + "MARK" + end / "IS" + "CIRCLE" + "X" + end / "STRAIGHT" + "X" + end / "NO" + "DOT" + end / "IF" + "CIRCLE" + "CUT" + "WIRE" + "THREE" + end. Mute sent nothing this round and will hear my relay now. No cut happens yet: the only cut proposal (wire three, red) is unconfirmed by Mute's repeat, and now it must also survive the corrected plate identity.
